chunks: Saʿd, from Abū Jaʿfar, from Mūsā ibn al-Qāsim al-Bajalī and Abū Qatādah, from ʿAlī ibn Jaʿfar, from his brother Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar عليهما السلام, who said:
“It is upon the Imam to raise his hand in the salat (prayer); it is not upon anyone other than him to raise his hand in the salat (prayer).”

Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan said: The meaning in this report is that the act of the Imam has greater merit and stronger emphasis than the act of the one praying behind him, even though the act of the one praying behind him also contains merit, as we have explained previously.

key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: the ritual salat (prayer) in which this act occurs
key_terms.الْإِمَامِ: the prayer leader whose act is more emphasized in this report
key_terms.الْمَأْمُومِ: the follower praying behind the Imam
key_terms.تَأْكِيدًا: stronger emphasis or stress in legal-religious practice
key_terms.فَضْلًا: extra merit or virtue attached to the act
key_terms.يَرْفَعَ يَدَهُ: to raise his hand during salat (prayer)

ai.seo_question: Is raising the hand in salat (prayer) مخصوص to the Imam or recommended for the follower as well?
ai.summary: This report states that raising the hand in salat (prayer) is especially emphasized for the Imam. Shaykh al-Ṭūsī explains that the narration indicates greater merit and emphasis for the Imam’s act, while the follower’s doing so also remains meritorious.
